subject: ela
name: English Language Arts
course: Informational Analysis, Textual Evidence & Opinion Writing
title: Grade 3 English Language Arts: Informational Analysis, Textual Evidence & Opinion Writing
overview: Grade 3 English Language Arts immerses students in literary and informational texts, developing close reading comprehension, evidence-based writing, academic vocabulary, and collaborative discourse.
competencies: Read grade-level literary and informational texts with fluency, accuracy, and deep comprehension.
Cite specific textual evidence to substantiate answers, inferences, and central theme analyses.
Write clear, organized opinion, informative, and narrative compositions using standard grammar conventions.
Participate actively in collaborative discussions, expressing ideas clearly and building upon others' contributions.

modules.title: Close Reading, Central Message & Text Evidence
modules.description: Answering questions by citing direct textual evidence, identifying character motivations, and distinguishing literal from non-literal language.

topics.title: Citing Text Evidence in Literature
topics.description: Referring explicitly to the text when asking and answering comprehension questions.

topics.title: Literal vs. Non-Literal Language & Idioms
topics.description: Interpreting figurative idioms, metaphors, and sensory descriptions in context.

modules.title: Informational Text Structures & Author's Point of View
modules.description: Analyzing cause/effect, compare/contrast, and chronological text structures, and evaluating author perspective.

topics.title: Informational Text Structures
topics.description: Recognizing sequence, cause/effect, and problem/solution transition keywords.

topics.title: Author's Point of View vs. Reader's View
topics.description: Distinguishing one's own point of view from that of the author or historical speaker.

modules.title: Structured Multi-Paragraph Writing & Research Inquiry
modules.description: Drafting multi-paragraph opinion and informative essays with clear introductions, grouped reasons, and transition words.

topics.title: Opinion Essay Workshop
topics.description: Formulating thesis statements, providing logical supporting evidence, and concluding effectively.

topics.title: Informational Explanatory Reports
topics.description: Conducting guided research, grouping related ideas, and integrating diagrams/illustrations.
